newsitem.title: JAPAN: Digital watches bring profit windfall for Casio.
newsitem.headline: Digital watches bring profit windfall for Casio.

text.p: Watch and calculator maker Casio Computer Co Ltd reported strong growth in its half-year profit on Thursday, helped by booming sales of digital watches.
Casio unveiled a 33 percent jump in its parent current profit to 4.17 billion yen ($37.2 million) for the six months to September from the same period a year earlier.
For the full business year ending on March 31, 1997, the leading digital watch manufacturer forecast its profit would soar just under 30 percent to eight billion yen ($71.4 million).
Sales of multi-functional digital watches, which store data such as telephone numbers, and sturdy "G-Shock" watches, popular among younger consumers, contributed to overall sales, it said.

"In the digital watch division, G-shock as well as the Baby-G model for ladies were a great hit both at home and abroad," the company said in a statement. Half-year profit from that division alone marked a solid 31.4 percent leap year-on-year.
Current profit is pretax and includes gains or losses on non-operating activities such as stock investment.

Casio's half-year sales grew 5.3 percent to 167.5 billion yen ($1.49 billion). It said domestic sales slipped 1.9 percent to 91.3 billion yen ($815 million), but overall exports grew 15.5 percent to 76.1 billion yen ($679 million) thanks to the yen's relative weakness compared with last year, which makes Japanese exports competitive abroad. The figures were rounded.
Sales of personal handy phones were also good. Personal handy phones are a type of cellular phone developed in Japan that are simpler and cheaper than conventional mobile phones.
In the audio visual sector, the company continued to enjoy good sales of digital cameras, introduced in late 1994/95 at comparatively cheaper prices than its rivals.

Casio said it is likely to ship 800,000 digital cameras in the full business year, lower than the initially planned one million units due to a delay in key electric parts, but was still hoping to achieve its target.

"If conditions allow, we still hope to dominate half of the global digital camera market this year, by shipping a total of one million units for the year," a company spokesman said. It forecast total digital camera demand in Japan at one million units and another one million in overseas markets this year.
